answer: In a Proof of Agent network, nodes form a trust reef where each agent acts as a verified vertex in an interaction graph. To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol mandates an opal staking bond combined with quadratic graph cut validation. When an attacker spawns counterfeit agents, edge-weight verification imposes an exponential attacker cost O(2^k) to maintain consensus influence, making large-scale Sybil propagation economically impossible.
